title: Each Answerable for Their Own Sin

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Parents are not to be put to death for their children, nor children put to death for their parents; each will die for their own sin. - Deut 24:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God establishes a vital principle of justice, each person is responsible for their own sin. Parents were not to be executed for their children's crimes, nor children for their parents'. This protected against the ancient practice of punishing whole families for one person's wrongdoing. God's justice is precise and personal, it holds the actual guilty party responsible, not the innocent.

This reveals the fairness at the heart of God's justice. He does not lump people together or punish the innocent for another's sin. Each individual stands before God accountable for their own choices and actions. This is both sobering and reassuring, sobering because we cannot blame others for our own sin, and reassuring because we will not be condemned for what someone else has done.

The prophet Ezekiel later expanded on this truth, declaring that the soul who sins is the one who will die, each answerable for their own life before God (Ezek 18:20). This makes the gospel all the more astonishing. Though each of us is personally guilty before God and deserving of judgment, Jesus, the truly innocent One, willingly took our punishment upon Himself. He, who had no sin of His own, bore ours, so that we, the guilty, could go free (2 Cor 5:21). The principle of personal responsibility makes Christ's substitution for us all the more amazing. How does personal accountability deepen your gratitude for what Christ has done?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take responsibility for your own choices before God?
2. How does personal accountability sober and reassure you?
3. How does Christ bearing your guilt amaze you afresh?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am accountable to You for my own life. Thank You that Jesus, the innocent One, bore my guilt so I could go free. Amen.
